elements.content: Communication Goal: I can ask about prices, compare options, and choose what to buy.

Lesson overview:
- Level: A0 General English
- Unit: Unit 7. Shopping
- Time: 60 min (Essential) / 90 min (Expanded) / 120 min (Full Workshop)
- Focus: Shopping day
- Materials: Price cards, toy till, play money, receipts, COSYmanuals 'how much' and 'demonstratives' pages.
By the end of this lesson, you can:

• ask about prices
• compare options with one/ones and too + adjective
• choose and pay for an item

Which word belongs to the previous lesson?
Core Active Vocabulary (18 items):

buy — to get something with money. Example: I want to buy a gift.
cost — to have a price. Example: How much does it cost?
pay — to give money for something. Example: I pay by card.
cash — money in notes and coins. Example: Can I pay in cash?
card — a plastic payment card. Example: I pay by card.
price — the amount of money something costs. Example: The price is twenty euros.
shop — a place where you buy things. Example: The shop opens at nine.
cheap — not expensive. Example: This bag is cheap.
expensive — costing a lot of money. Example: That phone is expensive.
receipt — a paper that shows you paid. Example: Keep the receipt.
one — a single item already mentioned. Example: I'll take this one.
ones — the plural pronoun for things already mentioned. Example: The small ones are cheap.
too — more than is good or possible. Example: It's too expensive.
choose — to decide between options. Example: I choose the blue one.
option — one of several choices. Example: The red one is a good option.
try — to test something before you buy it. Example: Can I try this shirt?
size — how big or small something is. Example: What size are you?
colour — red, blue, green, and so on. Example: What colour is your bag?
Essential Chunks & Functional Collocations:

• How much is it? (asking about price)
• How much does it cost? (asking about price)
• I'll pay by card. (choosing a payment method)
• Can I have a receipt, please? (asking for proof of payment)
• The red one is nice. The small ones are cheap. (using one/ones)
• It's too expensive. / It's too small. (using too + adjective)
• I'll take this one. (choosing an item)
Vocabulary practice: choose the correct word.

elements.content: Grammar Focus: Use 'How much...?' to ask about price.

Form:
How much is it? Prices and cost: How much is it? How much are they? How much does it cost? It costs... / They cost... / It's...

Examples:
• How much is this shirt?
• It's twenty pounds.
• How much do these shoes cost?
• They cost forty euros.
Controlled practice: choose the correct form.
___ much is this bag?
It ___ twenty euros.
How much ___ these shoes?
How much does it ___?
Substitution drill: say the sentence with the new words.

• How much is ...?
• How much are ...?
• It costs ...
Question-answer practice: ask and answer with your partner.

• How much is your phone?
• How much are your shoes?
• How much does a coffee cost in your city?
Personalised production: use the structure about your own life.

• Write three price questions and answers.
• Write three sentences about the prices of things you want to buy.
Reading: Shopping day

Today is shopping day! How much is this bag? It is twenty pounds. How much do those shoes cost? They cost forty pounds. That shirt is cheap, but this jacket is too expensive. I like the blue one, but the black ones are nicer. The small ones are too small. I'll take the blue one. I'll pay by card. Can I have a receipt, please? Yes, of course.
How much is the bag?
Why doesn't the writer take the small ones?
Listening: listen to the dialogue and answer the questions.

A: How much is this shirt?
B: It's fifteen pounds.
A: And how much do these shoes cost?
B: They cost thirty pounds. The black ones are cheaper.
A: The black ones are nice, but they are too small. I'll take the blue ones.
B: Good choice. Cash or card?
A: Card, please. Can I have a receipt?
Which shoes does the customer take?
Why doesn't the customer take the black ones?
Speaking task: Compare three items in a shop. Ask about prices and choose one using one/ones and too + adjective.

• How much is your phone?
• Do you prefer cash or card?
• Do you compare prices before you buy?
• What do you do when something is too expensive?
• Do you keep receipts?
Role-play: You are at a market. Ask about three prices, compare the options, and choose one item.
Work in pairs. Take turns. Use at least five target words and one target grammar structure. Then swap roles.
Writing task: Write a shopping dialogue with price questions, one/ones, and too + adjective.
Model: A: How much is ...? B: It's ... A: The ... one is too ... I'll take ...
